# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Morgan Iverson**
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Wellpoint — Appeals Department
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**RE:** Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated August 25, 2026
**Member:** Morgan Iverson
**Member ID:** W192391130
**Reference number:** POC-D5B17E1A47-69764
**Service denied:** Partial knee replacement, CPT 27446
**Governing policy:** Carelon Joint Surgery (MSK02-1125.1), https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/joint-surgery-2025-11-15/

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of the partial knee replacement (CPT 27446) that my surgeon, Dr. Duval, requested for me. The notice dated August 25, 2026 states that the clinical records do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. I am asking Wellpoint to reconsider that decision, because the records that were already submitted document exactly the conservative care the plan's own guideline describes.

I am writing about the criteria in the Carelon Joint Surgery guideline identified above. Below, I have set the plan's own language next to what is in my chart.

## The plan's criteria and what my records show

**1. Length of conservative care.** The guideline states:

> "Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-surgical conservative management (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4)"

My records show supervised physical therapy from April 22, 2026 through July 15, 2026 — a full 12 weeks, with 20 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note. In addition, my imaging of July 10, 2026 was read as Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medially, which is the finding the guideline names in its parenthetical exception. I met the 12-week requirement and also have the grade the guideline treats as an exception to it.

**2. The required combination of treatments.** The guideline states:

> "Conservative management 1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

My care included both parts. For physical therapy, the guideline states:

> "Physical therapy requirement includes ANY of the following: Physical therapy rendered by a qualified provider of physical therapy services Supervised home treatment program that includes ALL the following: Participation in a patient-specific or tailored program Initial active instruction by MD/DO/PT with redemonstration of patient ability to perform exercises Compliance (documented or by clinician attestation on follow-up evaluation)"

I completed supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, 20 visits over 12 weeks, discharged July 15, 2026. That satisfies the first option the guideline lists.

For the complementary treatment, the guideline states:

> "Complementary conservative treatment requirement includes ANY of the following: Anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics 2 Adjunctive medications such as nerve membrane stabilizers or muscle relaxants 2 Intra-articular corticosteroid injection(s) 2 Alternative therapies such as activity modification, and/or a trial period of rest (e.g., from the aggravating/contributing factors), where applicable"

My records document two of these, not just one: NSAIDs for six months with inadequate relief, and an intra-articular corticosteroid injection on May 1, 2026 that gave only about four weeks of partial relief.

**3. Failure of conservative management.** The guideline states:

> "Failure of conservative management requires ALL the following: Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation More invasive forms of therapy are being considered"

All three are in my chart. I completed the full course described above. My symptoms did not significantly improve: I have had 14 months of progressive knee pain that is not relieved by rest, the NSAIDs gave inadequate relief, and the injection helped only briefly. And a more invasive option is now being considered — that is precisely the surgery my surgeon requested and that Wellpoint denied.

**4. Documentation of symptoms, function, and treatments.** The guideline states:

> "Clinical notes describing symptom duration and severity, specific functional limitations related to symptoms, and type and duration of all therapeutic measures provided. If conservative management is not appropriate, the reason must be clearly documented."

My notes describe symptom duration (14 months, progressive), specific functional limitations (I cannot climb stairs without assistance, and I wake three to four times a night because of the pain), and the type and duration of every therapeutic measure I tried, with dates: physical therapy 4/22/2026–7/15/2026, NSAIDs for six months, and the injection on 5/1/2026.

On severity, the guideline states:

> "Reporting symptom severity – Severity of pain and its associated impact on activities of daily living (ADLs) and instrumental ADLs (IADLs) are key factors in determining the need for intervention. For purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated at least 3 out of 10 in intensity and associated with inability to perform ADLs and/or IADLs."

My inability to climb stairs without assistance and my repeated nightly awakenings are the kind of impact on daily activities this section describes. If a numeric pain rating is needed for the file, please see [pain rating as documented in the office notes, if recorded], and my treating office can supply it.

**5. Reevaluation.** The guideline states:

> "Clinical reevaluation – In most cases, reevaluation should include a physical examination. Direct contact by other methods, such as telephone communication or electronic messaging, may substitute for in-person evaluation when circumstances preclude an office visit. Clinical reevaluation must be done in reasonable proximity to the anticipated date of service such that the patient's condition would be unlikely to change by the date of service."

I was examined in person, with positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain, and I was discharged from physical therapy on July 15, 2026. The anticipated date of service is [date of service, if scheduled]. If a more recent examination would help, I am willing to be seen again promptly.

**6. Imaging.** Although imaging was not the reason given for this denial, the guideline states:

> "Imaging evidence of significant joint destruction and cartilage loss, defined as diffuse modified Outerbridge grade III – IV or Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 – 4, isolated to the medial or lateral knee compartment with no degenerative changes in the opposite compartment"

and

> "Imaging reports obtained within the past 12 months describing the degree of cartilage damage as determined by either or both of the following methods: X-ray report or provider interpretation of x-rays that utilizes or can be correlated with the Kellgren-Lawrence grading system of osteoarthritis MRI report from a radiologist that utilizes or can be correlated with the modified Outerbridge or similar classification system related to articular cartilage injury and osteoarthritis"

My MRI of July 10, 2026 — well within the past 12 months — shows full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medially.

**7. Other guideline elements.** The guideline also addresses alignment and ligament status, including:

> "Less than 10 degrees of fixed varus deformity for medial UKA"

and

> "Intact anterior cruciate ligament or documentation of stable knee examination (UKA may done with concurrent ACL reconstruction if all other criteria are met)"

These measurements are not stated in the summary I have in front of me. If Wellpoint needs them, I ask that they be requested from Dr. Duval's office, which has my complete chart, rather than have the request denied for a document that was never asked for: [measured varus/valgus alignment and ACL/ligament examination findings, to be supplied by the surgeon's office].

## What I am asking for

I understand that the Carelon Joint Surgery guideline contains further conditions and lists that were not reproduced in the material I received. Because the denial notice does not identify which specific criterion I failed to meet, I ask that Wellpoint, as part of this appeal:

1. Overturn the denial and authorize CPT 27446 as requested by Dr. Duval; or
2. If the denial is maintained, identify in writing the exact criterion from the Carelon Joint Surgery guideline that my records did not satisfy, and state what documentation would satisfy it.

I also request a copy of the clinical review criteria used in my case, the reviewer's credentials and specialty, and the complete file relied on in making this determination.

My surgeon has documented that this procedure is medically necessary for me. Every week that this is delayed is another week of stairs I cannot climb on my own and nights I do not sleep through. I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day window stated in my denial notice — that is, by **February 21, 2027** — and I am sending it to the appeal address printed on that notice. (Anthem/Elevance appeal addresses are plan- and state-specific; I can also be reached through my member account at anthem.com or the Sydney Health app, or at the number on the back of my ID card, if anything further is needed from me.)

Thank you for taking a fresh look at this. Please contact me if any additional records would help.

Sincerely,

**Morgan Iverson**
